ateret-zekenim/1:_: One may not knead, etc. One should point the lamed in shelanu with kamatz and not patach, for otherwise it speaks of him alone like u-lanu in Gibeah (so too in his Shulchan Aruch). If one kneaded, it is forbidden only in eating; but in benefit it is permitted immediately before it comes to leavening. Even where it is impossible, one should not permit even b'dieved since there is concern for becoming chametz — unlike what Shulchan Aruch wrote to be lenient in a time of pressure. However, water drawn while it was still day and left overnight, or drawn after the beginning of the night and left overnight, is permitted even l'chatchila.
baer-heitev/1:א: Close to bein ha shemashot. By right one should draw them at bein ha shemashot itself; and since not everyone knows how to measure bein ha shemashot, therefore one draws them close to bein ha shemashot after sunset (before moonrise). B'dieved, if one drew them while it was still day or drew after the beginning of the night, it appears from the words of the later authorities that one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours; and in responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than to draw early. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay — see Ateret Zekenim; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham. Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ד: On the night of the 5th. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor on Friday evening when they need to draw at bein ha shemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov (and if not for preparation it would certainly be permitted, for all shevut is permitted at bein ha shemashot) — therefore they draw on the night of the 5th that belongs to the 6th day, Beit Yosef; if so, also those who bake on the second day of Yom Tov are forbidden to draw at bein ha shemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need to draw on the eve of the 14th. It appears to me that if he forgot to draw on the night of the 5th he may draw on Friday while it is still day on this Erev Pesach. Or he may command a gentile to draw at bein ha shemashot — see siman 307. Or he may take water drawn in his house even though not drawn for the sake of the mitzvah, since it is impossible otherwise. Magen Avraham; see Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ז: Designated. One should say at the time of drawing for the sake of matzah of the mitzvah — Maharil and Mahariv; and Maharil wrote further that some are accustomed to take designated water each night independently.
baer-heitev/2:ב: Pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even though there is concern they were drawn by day or at night — Kaf HaChayim, Ateret Zekenim. And in Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 97 he is lenient regarding rainwater collected from the air at night.
baer-heitev/3:ב: Lukewarm. That is, like the warmth of saliva; and it is explained in Tur and Beit Yosef that in benefit it is permitted for everyone even if one kneaded with hot water.
baer-heitev/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two, Beit Yosef; but Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote it is nullified in the majority, and so too in Yoreh De'ah siman 98, Magen Avraham; and it is implied from the words of the poskim that if it became mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically that it became mixed before kneading. (And Kaf HaChayim ruled in the name of his brother-in-law the Gaon, may he rest in Eden, that he permitted even at the time of kneading.) And Ateret Zekenim raised that b'dieved one may permit even in such a case. And Magen Avraham wrote it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not because of prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so, it is permitted to cool them l'chatchila — requires study. And Kaf HaChayim wrote the same applies to copper-kettle water — this cooling helps according to all — and so too Ateret Zekenim.
baer-heitev/5:א: Salt. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape the faces of the matzah in salt water and return them to the oven as on chol ha'moed. And specifically on chol ha'moed scraping is permitted, but on the first two nights it is forbidden — see Taz.
baer-heitev/5:ב: To forbid. That is, in eating; but in benefit it is certainly permitted. And if he put a little salt in it, if it is baked immediately it is permitted in eating, for a little salt does not heat it entirely — Magen Avraham. And all this if one kneaded with water; but if one kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
baer-heitev/6:ב: Matzah. And in Rambam it implies it is rich matzah. And for everyone one must eat a kezayit of matzah aside from spices. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes the entire dough chametz; and the same applies to a little lime — Darkei Moshe. It appears specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted. It appears ginger is treated like pepper, and possibly the same for anise and saffron. Magen Avraham and Ateret Zekenim ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices except pepper. And even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as written in s.k. 15; and so Bach, Ateret Zekenim, and Kaf HaChayim. Dough kneaded in wine into which beer became mixed — Hagahot Beit Yosef wrote that since there is no water there is no need to be particular — Ateret Zekenim; see responsum Darkei Noam Orach Chayim siman 6 and Ginat Veradim general rule 4 siman 9.
beer-hagolah/3:ד: Tur in the name of Mahariv and Maharitz Gaon — according to his explanation they disagree regarding water that was not left overnight; and likewise Rambam in chapter 5
beer-hagolah/3:ה: Tur according to Rashi's explanation, and likewise the Rosh there
beer-hagolah/6:א: Rambam chapter 5, Rosh, and Mordechai end of chapter 3 of Pesachim — from that which is in Menachot 23
beur-hagra/1:א: (1) One may not knead. Rashi wrote the reason: because in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower parts of the sky and the springs boil, as written 94b. And R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote the reason: because at night the sun travels below the ground — see there; and their words appear from our words that by day springs are cold and at night they boil. And Rif explained what is written at the end of chapter Kol Sha'ah: the drawn water that was drawn on that day — and it is implied from his words that drawing from the attached source heats them and requires overnight standing; therefore he calls them drawn water because drawing heats them — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi. According to Rashi, whatever stood 12 hours detached, even from morning until evening, is sufficient; and according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, specifically when it was not attached at night; and according to his words, even after the beginning of the night it is permitted to knead with them provided it was not attached at the beginning of the night. But R' Yehuda bar Natan wrote, and likewise Semak in the name of R' Yitzchak and Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 5, that the end of the night causes cooling because the north wind blows from midnight onward until dawn, as written at the beginning of Berachot; and it is cold, as written in Bava Batra 25b: from adulterers comes this north wind; therefore one must leave them the entire night — and so Rashba that one must leave them the entire night.
beur-hagra/1:ב: Between, etc. For Rashi, specifically cistern and spring water; but in rivers there is no concern, for specifically springs boil, as written in the Gemara: springs boil — and the reason is they are close to their exit from the source; and likewise according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's explanation. And Rashi wrote: nevertheless one should not breach the fence of the early authorities; but according to Rif's explanation it is forbidden by law.
beur-hagra/1:ג: While it is still day, etc. For R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote that according to R' Eliezer of Metz one must draw them specifically at bein ha shemashot so they remain attached all day, for by day springs are cold as written — and so Semak; and some are stringent to draw between day and night; and some forbid when drawn while it is still day even if left overnight afterward. Semak there rejected this because he mentioned only overnight standing — implying one need not be concerned when they were drawn, only that they stood overnight; and Beit Yosef rejected R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words and explained "while it is still day or bein ha shemashot" means only that one should not draw after the beginning of the night; but Beit Yosef was concerned for the stringent view and wrote close to bein ha shemashot and not while it is still day. However, from the conclusion of all poskim and from the language of the Gemara it is implied like Shulchan Aruch's view; and likewise from Rif's language that he wrote they were drawn on that day.
beur-hagra/1:ד: And one may not knead, etc. To be concerned for R' Yehuda bar Natan's view as above.
beur-hagra/1:ו: And if the weather. To cool them specifically according to Rif's explanation, that the reason they became warm when drawn and need cooling.
beur-hagra/1:ח: And even. As written end of chapter 3 of Yoma: a cloudy day is entirely sun — for Rava's exposition: a woman should not knead, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ט: And if not. As Rambam and Shulchan Aruch siman 259 seif 8 wrote — see what is written there.
beur-hagra/1:כ: When it falls. For Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov, as written at the beginning of Yom Tov; and he follows his reasoning that he ruled one must draw them specifically at bein ha shemashot or close to it — see Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/1:פ: And it is customary to take. As written in Maggid Mishneh regarding Chanukah — and specifically in earthenware; see siman 453 seif 3.
beur-hagra/2:א: Seif 2: some say water. See Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3: one may not knead. Pesachim 42a — and they are equal that there is no, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ד: Whether with water. According to Rif's explanation, drawn water means water not left overnight, and the question also refers to water not left overnight.
beur-hagra/3:ו: And some say that b'shogeg, etc. For one transgressed intentionally as written chapter 2 of Yoma 17: they asked — if one transgressed and baked, etc.; and there it deals with intentional as written 99b, etc.; provided he does not deceive, etc.; this case of deception is different, etc.; 99b: one who cooks, etc.; and the first reasoning holds we also find one transgressed b'shogeg, as written chapter 3 of Shabbos: they asked — if one transgressed and stayed, what? And according to Rif's explanation there they asked regarding metsamek ve-yafeh whether it is forbidden b'shogeg — see Tosafot there; and proof from the pastries of Eretz Yisrael; and we are not concerned for such a case; but Rashi and Rosh rejected there and said because it is close to intentional; and all the more so for those who baked in our presence — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi siman 226.
beur-hagra/4:_: Seif 4: water not, etc. And some say one in two, rather in majority as Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote; and the reason: since the majority is cold it cools — as Tosafot wrote Shabbos 42a s.v. noten; rather it appears as Rabbenu Tam says, etc.
beur-hagra/5:_: Seif 5: it is customary, etc. And even. They bring proof to forbid from what is written chapter 8 of Shabbos and in Gittin: matzah that is not salted; and in Chullin they said salted is like boiling and is like kneading in hot water — as above seif 3; and chapter 4 of Shabbos; and not regarding salt that adds vapor; and chapter 2 of Bava Batra: they distance salt because of heat — as written in the Gemara there. And this is what Baer Heitev wrote: and even b'dieved, etc.; and so Mordechai; and as above seif 3. But many poskim permit and reject their proofs: that which "not salted" means it lacks preparation like "not sharpened"; and that which "salted is like boiling" — they state explicitly only when it is not eaten because of its salt — see Yoreh De'ah siman 98 and siman 105; and likewise that of Shabbos and Bava Batra where there is much salt; and Rashba siman 224 that it is not like boiling but to absorb and extract, etc.; but to heat, etc. And Ran brings proof to permit from end of chapter Kol Sha'ah from what is written: and soaked in water and salt is forbidden — implying specifically when cooking it heats; but for bread, no — and so Rashba, except he wrote people are accustomed to be stringent.
beur-hagra/6:א: Seif 6: since it has. In the Gemara there they say specifically that he added flour to it; and Tosafot wrote this sugya argues on that of Zevachim where they said even though the majority is rice, etc. — majority of Torah law; and we rule like the sugya of Zevachim that taste in a kezayit in a place of Torah law obligates, as Tosafot wrote; and likewise Tur explained in Yoreh De'ah; and this is what Shulchan Aruch wrote: since, etc.
beur-hagra/6:ב: Nevertheless. The Ra'avad in chapter 12 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot forbids in cooked dishes that become chametz; and what is written in Menachot "seasoned," etc., and so in Tosefta and Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah — matzah seasoned is discussed when seasoning is after baking; but in Yerushalmi chapter 2 halachah 4 it is not so, for R' Simon in the name of R' Yehuda bar Levi said: that kezayit with which a person fulfills on the 15th of Nissan must not have liquid come into it, etc.; and it was taught: one fulfills with seasoned matzah even though it has no taste of grain — they thought to say seasoned means liquids; it was said seasoned means spiced; nuts — therefore permitted even before baking, for after baking rich matzah is not relevant; and as written siman 462 seif 4; and so Ra'avad in laws of matzah chapter 6 because of rich matzah it is forbidden.
beur-hagra/6:ג: And pepper. For it is not called spice as Tosafot wrote chapter 1 of Yoma in the name of Tosefta; and pepper is likewise as spice — see Tosafot Pesachim 105a s.v. atei, etc.; and it heats as written in Niddah: she ate pepper and saw — see there in Shulchan Aruch siman 129.
beur-hagra/6:ד: And likewise. As written chapter 3 of Shabbos and chapter 2 of Bava Batra.
biur-halacha/1:_: While it is still day — know that what Rama wrote in the gloss "close to bein ha shemashot" is not the Mechaber's view but his own view, as explained in Darkei Moshe; but for the Mechaber it is permitted l'chatchila to draw by day at any hour he wishes, provided he waits to knead with them until the morrow, as his view is explained in Beit Yosef; and so Gra, Peri Chadash, and Maamar Mordechai ruled as the main view; therefore Maamar Mordechai wrote that where there is some pressure one may fill by day while the day is still long, since according to Maran, may he rest in Eden, one may do so l'chatchila.
biur-halacha/3:א: Large kettle — see Mishna Berurah for the reason; see Peri Megadim that this applies only when the kettle is still somewhat lukewarm from having been moved from the fire a short time ago; if it cooled a long time, obviously there is no concern.
biur-halacha/3:ג: One may rely on them — Beit Chadash is stringent in all cases; but many acharonim wrote like Shulchan Aruch and Rama; and even according to Beit Chadash, if drawn from rivers one may rely to be lenient b'dieved b'shogeg, for it is known that according to Rashi the main law of water not left overnight applies specifically to springs; and likewise in mayim shelanu that were hot and one cooled them b'shogeg — one may be lenient even per Beit Chadash; and so Eliyah Rabbah.
biur-halacha/5:_: It is customary, etc., and this is correct — from this language it implies only l'chatchila but b'dieved one does not forbid; and therefore they did not decide that a little salt put in matzah for taste would heat the dough [for although we rule salted is like boiling, that is specifically when it is not eaten because of its salt], and he was not concerned for the stringent authorities only regarding l'chatchila; and Rama in the gloss who added to forbid even b'dieved follows his reasoning, for Darkei Moshe wrote that according to what Tur wrote later siman 462, salt water is fruit juice — if so it is fruit juice with water, and we rule they hasten to become chametz unless baked immediately; therefore he wrote here that even b'dieved it is forbidden — meaning if he was not careful to bake immediately [and the dough in his hands does not save from becoming chametz]; and so Kaf HaChayim ruled [and so implies Magen Avraham]: if he was careful to bake immediately, one does not forbid b'dieved the matzah for a little salt put in; and so Eliyah Rabbah. Know that according to what Rama wrote later siman 462 in Darkei Moshe, Tur deals only with salt dug from the ground, but salt made from sea water like mayim shelanu is water for everyone — if so one does not forbid b'dieved in our salt in any case (unless he put much salt), and even per Magen Avraham's objection there that Tur deals with our salt — nevertheless for the law Beit Yosef concludes in the passage name of Ran and Hagahot Maimoniyot unlike Tur, and so ruled in Shulchan Aruch that it is in the category of water; if so Rama's ruling to forbid even b'dieved applies only to salt dug from the ground if not baked immediately. Know further that even if we explain Rama in Shulchan Aruch who ruled anonymously to be stringent b'dieved, it is not because it is fruit juice but because he was concerned for the stringent view due to heating the dough — nevertheless for the law one should study, for many poskim are lenient as Gra wrote; and so is proven in Ritva's novellae on Pesachim that b'dieved one certainly should not be stringent with a little salt; and so Maharam Chalavah in his novellae to be lenient with little salt. Especially if he was shogeg, one certainly should not be stringent, for even kneading in hot water some poskim are lenient b'shogeg b'dieved as above seif 3 — all the more so here where many are certainly lenient one may rely — in my humble opinion. See Peri Chadash who disagrees with Rama and agrees with Mechaber to be lenient b'dieved.
chatam-sofer/1:_: (There in Taz s.k. 3) "He who keeps a mitzvah," etc. And that he did not bring this verse in the chapter Erev Pesachim daf 109b — because the rabbis would not institute a new mitzvah and rely on this, as Semak wrote siman 67 s.k. 2 in such a case — see there.
chatam-sofer/2:_: In Mechaber seif 5 in the gloss "one should forbid" — Mishna Berurah; see my responsa part 6 Orach Chayim siman 123.
chok-yaakov/1:א: Or at bein ha shemashot. The main time to draw is between sunset and nightfall before the moon shines on the ground — so too Maharil; see above siman 261 for the measure of bein ha shemashot. Since not everyone knows how to measure bein ha shemashot, one draws close to bein ha shemashot after sunset. B'dieved, if drawn while it is still day or drawn after the beginning of the night, it appears from the later authorities one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours. In responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss — see above seif 3. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than before. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay, for overnight standing is not mentioned explicitly in the Talmud — end quote; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/1:ג: And when carrying water under the open sky. This refers to the above that he wrote it is good to place them under the ceiling so that if he forgets to bring them in at dawn the sun will not shine on them. Therefore he also wrote: be careful also when carrying water by day under the open sky to the kneading house to cover it with a cloth so they will not become warm, as Semag and Semak wrote and Terumat HaDeshen siman 115 explicitly; and so Levush explained it deals by day — in the evening hour when they draw, since the sun already set, one need not cover them at all; it is only custom and extra caution lest something heating fall in, as Terumat HaDeshen wrote there. All this is simple and clear, unlike Magen Avraham who explained it refers to the time of drawing.
chok-yaakov/1:ה: Eve of the 13th, meaning Thursday night. For on Thursday night one is concerned lest he draw before Friday sunset or delay and violate Shabbos — so is the language of Mordechai end of the first chapter of Pesachim; from this it is implied b'dieved if he forgot to draw on the night of the 13th he may draw on Friday while it is still day close to bein ha shemashot or even at bein ha shemashot, for we are not concerned for Shabbos violation, for anything that is due to shevut they did not decree against at bein ha shemashot in a place of mitzvah, as explained above siman 261 and Shaarei Teshuvah there. However from Rokeach siman 265 and as brought by later authorities who wrote: when the 14th falls on Shabbos they draw on the night of the 13th from the river or well and do not draw from the cistern in his courtyard on Shabbos for kneading because he needs much and it appears like filling his garden and ruin as in Eruvin 104 — end quote — it appears that even b'dieved drawing is forbidden; and in truth Rokeach's words seem astonishing, for what prohibition is there, since it appears like filling — for there it is explained specifically via a wheel it is forbidden because he draws much and draws easily; and even with our wheel some permit as explained above siman 338 seif 16 — all the more so what they draw now for an individual in his house one or two buckets, which is a small matter, and also at bein ha shemashot where they did not decree shevut. If so, what prohibition is there? Rokeach's words can be answered with difficulty that his intent is if he wants to draw on Shabbos itself, as somewhat implied in his language, and not at bein ha shemashot; and it deals when they want to draw much for the courtyard — but not when forgotten for an individual, permitted to draw one or two buckets in his courtyard at bein ha shemashot or even in the river where carrying is permitted (however from later authorities who brought Rokeach it does not imply so). More plausible is concern for preparing from Shabbos to Yom Tov: (found in Shaarei Teshuvah siman 7 permission via small vessels and many people for this reason does not help). This concern is also in Beit Yosef and Magen Avraham, and they conclude one who forgot to draw on the night of the 5th should draw on Friday while it is still day, or command a gentile at bein ha shemashot, or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for the mitzvah since impossible otherwise — end quote; and it is better to draw oneself or via agent that day close to bein ha shemashot where there is no prohibition concern like other ways — see above s.k. 1 and responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 who wrote: the custom spread not to knead matzah after Shabbos except with water drawn on the eve of the 6th, for one can limit drawing at bein ha shemashot unlike two bein ha shemashot of Erev Shabbos; and what he wrote: where there is custom one should not be lenient unless pressure or great loss — end quote; nevertheless where there is no custom one should not be stringent and should not act as he wrote.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: To draw from wells. Maharil wrote: it is a good custom first to clean and purify the spring; and if impossible to clean all of it because of many water sources, nevertheless draw much water from it before drawing. And all cisterns in houses — generally much water was drawn in them to clean vessels for Pesach days — end quote; and in Shaarei Knesset HaGedolah: our custom is to filter water through a white cloth so nothing falls in — end quote. All this is only stringency l'chatchila — see above siman 457 s.k. 12 and siman 467 seif 12.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: Nevertheless l'chatchila it is good to place iron in them. Take new iron and hang it on a rope — Maharil and later authorities. Magen Avraham wrote in Darkei Moshe in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot: on all other days of the year one places salt or a seal — end quote. Taz wrote: nevertheless it appears that on other nights if he did not place iron to guard from tekufah he may discard them if he can easily be without those waters, unlike these waters of matzah of the mitzvah where it is forbidden to discard, for it appears contemptuous of the verse "He who keeps a mitzvah knows no evil" — end quote; and similarly Maharshal in his explanation to Semag; and the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek objected that his words imply only matzah of the mitzvah permits keeping the water, but even for other matzot one need not be particular about tekufah if one died; nevertheless he concludes in the name of Agudah that even for matzah of the mitzvah one permits only when impossible to borrow mayim shelanu in that city. It appears simple that even Agudah who is stringent speaks only in a small city with few people, but in a large city one is certainly not obligated to go door to door for water, only among neighbors and acquaintances — and so implies Taz's language that even all year one should not be stringent if he cannot easily be without that water — all the more so these waters; and the custom is to be lenient in every regard.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: Also forbidden for a gentile to draw. That is l'chatchila; and so explicit in Maharil that it is extra stringency l'chatchila; and so Shlah.
chok-yaakov/1:ט: And it is customary to take designated water. One says at the time of drawing for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah — Maharil and Mahariv siman 193; and Maharil wrote further that some take designated water each night independently.
chok-yaakov/1:י: New earthenware vessels, etc. In all books of Shulchan Aruch it is written thus in the name of Kol Bo, but I did not find it in his words. Magen Avraham wrote: Mateh Moshe wrote one should not take a vessel that had fruit juice, for fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz. (It appears to me through boiling it is permitted.) Also one should not take a copper vessel that heats — end quote; however I have seen practice kneading in copper troughs — end Magen Avraham. In truth one can distinguish: mayim shelanu require cooling, and in copper perhaps they do not cool — unlike for kneading; see gloss in minhagim forbidding drawing in copper too — so practice; b'dieved do not forbid — and so Ateret Zekenim siman 459; and so appears from what is written seif 3 on thick copper rim.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: Unless in a time of pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even if there is concern they were drawn by day or at night; see Beit Yosef and R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Bach siman 7; see what is written above s.k. 1 and s.k. 5 in the name of Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/3:א: One may not knead in hot water. Levush wrote: even if left overnight all night and heated only by the sun — thus his intent: even mayim shelanu, as long as they are still hot, it is forbidden to knead with them; unlike if they are cold before us, for which overnight water is needed to remove heat from the sun, as explained in the Talmud and poskim; and the same for copper-kettle water if cooled, as poskim and Mechaber imply who wrote "and water inside is lukewarm" — specifically while still lukewarm. However in responsum of Rama siman 35 he wrote: copper-kettle water, even after cooling, should be forbidden, for an intentional transgressor — not to mention R' Eliezer of Metz, for even water not left overnight, cooling does not help — all the more so hot water; and even per Rashi in copper-kettle water there is no remedy; therefore we do not find any posek who wrote there is remedy for copper-kettle water — end quote. In truth the Mechaber's implication is not so — see Ateret Zekenim; and so the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek from Mahari Weil; the poskim did not need to write remedy because copper-kettle water is stated, and whatever cooled is no longer copper-kettle water; and since they are cold before us, what prohibition is there — and on the contrary I have heard that sometimes water that was boiled and cooled is colder than other water. What he wrote that for R' Eliezer of Metz cooling does not help for water not left overnight is not necessary — see Beit Yosef. Although Mahari Weil that the brother-in-law brought concludes: heaven forbid to contradict their words without proof — it appears he understood Levush's "even if left overnight" means even if cooled; therefore he did not come to contradict his words. In truth Levush's intent is simple as written; and proof is clear from Talmud and poskim and Mechaber who wrote specifically hot or lukewarm; one who wants to be stringent in any case has permission to permit b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/3:ב: That its copper is thick. Magen Avraham wrote: the same applies to earthenware.
chok-yaakov/3:ג: Lukewarm. That is, like warmth of saliva; Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah halachah 7: although in Menachot kneaded lukewarm and they guard lest they become chametz because priests are zealous — in matzah even priests should not knead lukewarm lest distinguish matzah from matzah — end quote; see Menachot 55a; explained in Tur and Beit Yosef: in benefit permitted for all even kneading in hot water.
chok-yaakov/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two; see Sefer Me'irat Einayim general rule 91 s.k. 6; see Magen Avraham; and it is implied from poskim brought in Beit Yosef that if mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically mixed before kneading. The rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek raised b'dieved to permit even in such a case — see above s.k. 16; Magen Avraham wrote permitted to mix them even l'chatchila to cool them — requires study; and the same for copper-kettle water this cooling helps according to all — so Ateret Zekenim; see s.k. 13. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape matzot faces with salt water and return to the oven as on Chol HaMoed; specifically on Chol HaMoed permitted to scrape, but on the first two nights forbidden (Ateret Zekenim).
chok-yaakov/5:_: One should forbid. That is in eating; but in benefit certainly permitted, for Mishna Berurah compared it to kneading in hot water. If he put a little salt, if baked immediately permitted in eating — end quote; and all this if kneaded with water; but if kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/6:א: Valid. Nevertheless one does not fulfill the obligation of matzah with it and one does not eat it on the first night as rich matzah, since according to many poskim one fulfills with it — see above siman 462 and 471.
chok-yaakov/6:ב: And pepper. Magen Avraham wrote even one grain forbids; specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted; ginger is treated like pepper; possibly the same for anise and saffron — end quote; the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices; and so appears to me primary, for poskim mentioned only pepper; and they say: good is sharp pepper — Aruch explains because it is sharper than all spices; if so one should not compare other spices; and even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as s.k. 18; and so Bach and Ateret Zekenim — they are equal.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] Bein ha shemashot, etc. Or close to bein ha shemashot (Rama). Bach wrote: if drawn while it was still day and left overnight, or drawn after the beginning of the night and left overnight, it is permitted even l'chatchila — until here. It appears to me specifically before midnight; but after midnight it is forbidden, for we rely on Semak that overnight standing is from midnight until dawn — and he was precise and wrote "after the beginning of the night." Also it appears to me that after dawn it is permitted immediately even though not yet twelve hours from drawing — and so Bach end of siman 4 explicitly; Chak Yaakov did not understand so. Semak wrote in Hagahot: it is proper to wait to knead until the day brightens much lest one err by moonlight.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] And when carrying, etc., under the air, etc. Requires study: if it deals with kneading, he already wrote at the end of the seif; if when drawing, he wrote one need not cover them. Perhaps here it deals at night when he wants to place them in an open place he should cover, for then he might forget tomorrow — no concern. People always leave them covered at night even under the ceiling, and we are not concerned they will heat from this covering; the reason appears to me we are concerned something might fall in; and although Terumat HaDeshen wrote this is extra caution, it appears that is when carrying from river to house while engaged with it; but where they stand all night there is more concern.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] One may knead only in mayim shelanu — even matzah not for the mitzvah, because of concern for leavening. Rashbatz in Ma'amar on chametz 30 and responsum part 2 siman 87; brought Birkei Yosef note 1, Kissei Eliyahu note 1, Sha'arei Teshuvah this section; also Rosh end chapter Kol Sha'ah and Maggid Mishneh chapter 5 law 11; Bach, Beit Yosef; Kol Bo 38a — so agreed geonim and most sages, not like R' Yitzchak Gikat; see Bach, Eliyah Rabbah note 1; also Raz note 1.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. One may knead only with mayim shelanu. Doubtful mayim shelanu — one should not knead with them; if he kneaded, permitted. Mahari Bueno — brought by Rav Mezbeach Adamah; see what Morenu, may he rest in Eden, wrote in the gloss seif 3 from Mechaber in Kuntres Acharon note 1.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) One who collected rainwater — permitted to knead matzah with it and no overnight standing is required according to all, provided he does not leave them where their coldness will dissipate. Radbaz part 5 siman 2002; brought by Birkei Yosef note 4, Shaarei Teshuvah note 9. However Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 97 distinguishes: if collected by day requires overnight; if collected at night no overnight required — see there; brought by Yad Aharon in Hagahot and Birkei Yosef there; see further below note 64 what is written on this — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (5) Permitted to knead in water a gentile said casually is ours in his house — presumption of prohibition does not apply and it is d'rabbanan; stringent see 462. Maharil in responsum 21 siman 103; Birkei Yosef note 5. It appears certainly one does not fulfill with these on the 15th, for no guarding; also for other matzot concern — perhaps something leavening fell in; in pressure permit through filtering — Sha'arei Teshuvah there.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. One may knead only with mayim shelanu — meaning ours in another vessel after drawing. Rashi explained (Pesachim 42a): because in Nissan days the springs are hot since the rainy season still applies, and in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky; therefore the whole world is cold and springs hot; therefore we leave overnight and they cool — end quote. Some explain the reason: because at night the sun travels under the earth and heats the springs; therefore their only remedy is not to be attached at night, as Beit Yosef explains — see there. In derashot of Maharil he wrote the water must cool 24 hours before kneading: 12 hours by day while attached in the well when the sun is far, and 12 hours at night after drawing — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And Rashi — we rule like R' Nachman there 94b: in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky; therefore the whole world is cold and springs boil. Rashi there: in the lower part of the sky, close to the ground, at the edges of the sphere; therefore the whole world is cold, for it travels only at the sides of the world; and springs boil — meaning near the water at the sides of the world from which springs come — end quote. Nissan is still considered rainy season. Therefore there is no difference between night and day — always in rainy season, day and night, it travels in the lower sky; only at night it travels in the vault of the sky and the sky separates between sun and earth, hence darkness on the earth; by day it travels in the hollow of the sky toward the earth, hence the earth is lit. Therefore no difference whether drawn by day or night — water is hot and needs 12 hours cooling; if drawn in the morning, permitted to knead with them in the evening after 12 hours. R' Yehuda uses mayim shelanu implying they draw in the evening and knead in the morning — common practice: people bake by day, therefore must leave all night and may bake immediately at dawn.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: And R' Eliezer of Metz — we rule like the admission of the sages of Israel to the sages of the nations there: no difference between summer and rainy season; always by day it travels below the sky (therefore it lights for us), and at night below the ground (therefore earth's thickness separates between sun and us, hence night darkens); therefore by day springs cold, at night boiling — at night the sun travels near the place springs issue; by day when the sun is far they cool. According to him, if drawn at bein ha shemashot, permitted to knead immediately, for they already cooled 12 hours attached by day. In this there is no dispute per R' Eliezer of Metz — only if drawn by day or night they disagree: R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi whether drawn day or night they have no remedy forever. Rabbeinu Yehuda challenged: if so why call them mayim shelanu? In any case if drawn at bein ha shemashot no overnight needed and permitted immediately; if drawn by day or night, overnight does not help — therefore Rabbeinu Yehuda: per R' Eliezer of Metz, if drawn by day they need overnight of the following night and it helps; if drawn at night they need the full night they were drawn and the day after and the night after. His reason and reasoning — see Beit Yosef who elaborated greatly. R' Yitzchak Saba's view is also like R' Eliezer of Metz here, for we rule like admission of sages of Israel; except where R' Eliezer of Metz holds if drawn at bein ha shemashot no overnight needed because they cooled 12 hours attached — R' Yitzchak Saba disagrees and requires 24 hours cooling; therefore draw at bein ha shemashot; then they cool 12 hours attached by day (for by day springs are cold) and need overnight all night and cool 12 hours detached (for at night the world is cold). Maharil leans like R' Yitzchak Saba. One should not be lenient to draw by day (meaning before close to bein ha shemashot, about half hour before) — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct; meaning per R' Eliezer of Metz not correct per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi even if left all night, for they have no remedy; but per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ד: In this all agree. Meaning R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda agree it is not correct per R' Eliezer of Metz to draw at night; they disagree: per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi they have no remedy forever; per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night drawn does not help; nevertheless overnight of the following night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: One may be lenient: first, one may rely on Rashi that 12 hours waiting suffices whether drawn by day or night as above; second, even R' Eliezer of Metz was stringent only l'chatchila when possible; when impossible, perhaps R' Eliyahu Mizrachi agrees to be lenient.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ז: Know Bach wrote further leniency per Raavan who holds for Rashi one does not need 12 hours at night but suffices until after dawn if the night was short. Authors ruled 12 hours for Rashi — fixed time by day if drawn in morning; in Nissan day and night are equal and night is 12 hours; therefore its measure by day equals places where in Nissan night is 12 hours — because we do not distinguish. But if drawn at evening bein ha shemashot, leaving the night as it is, even if short, permitted immediately at dawn — I copied his words to be a shield for people of the land who do not wait 12 hours and knead at dawn — they have whom to rely on; but most poskim did not write so and one should not be lenient. See siman 261 measure of bein ha shemashot; Magen Avraham wrote there it is about a quarter hour — see there; see here Taz s.v. regarding law, etc.; see Kaf HaChayim agreed with Magen Avraham that better to draw a little before bein ha shemashot than after — unlike Taz.
machatzit-hashekel/4:א: (s.k. 4) On the night of the 5th, etc. Explanation: for those who bake, etc. — meaning it is explained siman 458: when Pesach falls on Sunday one kneads Friday evening after chatzot; obviously one draws Thursday night. Rama needed to write this for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos, as Tur siman 458.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ג: See siman 7 one may rely on Rabbeinu Yehuda — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ה: See siman 307: shevut of shevut is permitted in a place of mitzvah; therefore permitted to command a gentile.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ו: And siman 464 — meaning although Rama wrote in this seif forbidden via gentile; he brought proof from siman 464 that kneading and baking are certainly forbidden via gentile, yet Magen Avraham wrote there when impossible otherwise permitted via gentile when Jew stands over — all the more so drawing. Or take water drawn in his house — meaning mayim shelanu even if not drawn for the mitzvah.
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: But, etc. — always boiling; therefore wells are preferable.
magen-avraham/1:א: Close to bein ha shemashot. By right one should draw at bein ha shemashot itself so water cools 12 hours attached by day when springs are cold, and 12 hours in the air at night as Maharil wrote; but since impossible to measure bein ha shemashot precisely, permitted to draw close to bein ha shemashot. One should not be lenient to draw by day, for per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct — all the more so not to draw at night, for in this all agree. Beit Yosef wrote: if drawn after beginning of night they have no remedy and the water is forbidden forever per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — end quote Darkei Moshe; Bach wrote b'dieved if drawn at night one may be lenient to knead by day; see siman 261 measure of bein ha shemashot.
magen-avraham/1:ד: Thursday night. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor Friday when they need bein ha shemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov — therefore draw Thursday night belonging to Friday (Beit Yosef); see siman 467; if so, also those baking on second day of Yom Tov forbidden to draw at bein ha shemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need eve of 14th; see siman 458. It appears if he forgot Thursday night he may draw Friday while still day on this Erev Pesach, or command gentile at bein ha shemashot — see siman 307 and 464; or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for mitzvah since impossible otherwise.
magen-avraham/1:ח: Or falling tekufah. And Yoreh De'ah siman 116 wrote there is danger only when drinking at the hour tekufah falls (and so Shulchan Aruch HaRav).
magen-avraham/1:י: Wooden vessel, etc. — the same for glazed earthenware; see siman 473 seif 3.
magen-avraham/3:א: Large kettle. The copper of the kettle retains heat (Rashi); it does not deal with water heated on the fire, for then even if completely cooled it is forbidden even not in the kettle — merely putting water in the kettle without fire is forbidden because the kettle retains heat; so Agur in his responsum (Rama siman 35).
magen-avraham/4:_: One in two. Implies less than that is not nullified (Beit Yosef); but Semag and Semak wrote nullified in majority, and so Yoreh De'ah siman 98; we rule see Ateret Zekenim; it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so permitted to cool l'chatchila — requires study.
magen-avraham/5:_: One should forbid. Thus Darkei Moshe; per his words siman 462 even b'dieved forbid; Mordechai: eating salted matzah like eating chametz — end quote; it appears if a grain of salt fell in, if baked immediately permitted as siman 462; if because of heating, rely on all that little salt does not heat entire dough — b'dieved siman 91.
magen-avraham/6:ב: Since it has. Implies one fulfills with it on the first nights; however in Rambam it implies rich matzah; and so Maggid Mishneh chapter 6.
magen-avraham/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes entire dough chametz; likewise a little lime (Darkei Moshe, Mahariv). It appears specifically kneaded into it; if fell on, remove and permitted. Ginger like pepper; possibly anise and saffron too. In hints it implies pepper permitted b'dieved; nevertheless do not be lenient — see above seif 65 regarding salt.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) Only with mayim shelanu — meaning overnight standing in a vessel after drawing. Rashi wrote in the Gemara: in Nissan days springs are hot because then the sun travels in the lower sky near earth and heats springs; some explain because at night the sun travels below the ground and heats springs; therefore sages forbade using them for kneading immediately upon taking from the ground [for they are like hot water forbidden for kneading as below seif 3] until they stand in vessels and cool from their heat; measure of standing in vessels and time of drawing from the well will be explained below.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) Close to bein ha shemashot — l'chatchila it is fitting and proper to draw at bein ha shemashot itself so water cools 12 hours attached by day when springs are cold and 12 hours in air at night; but since impossible to measure bein ha shemashot precisely, permitted to draw close to bein ha shemashot. One should not be lenient l'chatchila to draw much while still day — all the more so not after nightfall; nevertheless b'dieved if drawn much while still day one should not be stringent and may knead l'chatchila after overnight; see Biur Halacha. Likewise if drawn at night before chatzot, permitted to knead tomorrow l'chatchila, but must wait 12 hours from drawing.
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (8) For the cellar is warm — if placed in cellar or heated house it will be explained below in the gloss.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (9) Before sunrise — lest they heat from sun's heat; it deals when water stands outside where sun rises from there; if where he cannot see the sun's face, no concern — as siman 259 seif 1 — see there; however on cloudy day in every case must be careful to bring in before sunrise hour, for a cloudy day is entirely sun.
mishnah-berurah/1:נ: (14) One should draw, etc. — per Mechaber siman 458: when 14th falls on Shabbos, kneading Friday evening is no novelty; Rama's words speak to those who bake Pesach night at Motzei Shabbos, as Tur explains there.
mishnah-berurah/1:ס: (15) Meaning Thursday night — on Friday at bein ha shemashot they cannot draw, for Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov and bein ha shemashot is Shabbos doubt; drawing while still day close to bein ha shemashot is also improper lest he delay and do so on bein ha shemashot [and likewise those baking second Yom Tov night forbidden at bein ha shemashot of first Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need eve of 14th]. If forgot Thursday night, may draw Friday while still day even while day is long; all this applies to those baking many days before Pesach — when baking Sunday, l'chatchila prepare water Thursday night, b'dieved Friday while still day. If forgot to prepare while still day, may prepare at bein ha shemashot via gentile; some permit even via oneself.
mishnah-berurah/1:23: (23) For matzah of the mitzvah — one says at drawing for matzah of the mitzvah [later authorities].
mishnah-berurah/1:25: (25) Wooden vessel, etc. — likewise stone or coated earthenware (glazed); only if used only for water; if had fruit juice (all liquids except water for this law) beware drawing unless boiled first, for fruit juice mixed hastens to become chametz as siman 462; certainly forbid large barrels used for honey then washed for matzah in bakeries — absolute prohibition as fruit juice exudes. L'chatchila avoid copper even new — copper heats; b'dieved no concern even if water stood many days; even l'chatchila practice permits copper troughs — only beware drawing for water needs overnight cooling and in copper does not cool like other vessels.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (28) Pressure — nevertheless if he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house, better to take them even if concern they were drawn while still day or after beginning of night. Rainwater collected from air needs no overnight, for already cooled in air through descent; however if not kneading immediately, must not place where coldness will dissipate — as above seif 1.
mishnah-berurah/5:א: (40) It is customary not to, etc. — because some say salt heats dough and thereby eases leavening.
mishnah-berurah/5:ד: (43) One should forbid — Peri Chadash disagrees and holds one should not be stringent b'dieved with little salt; appears if he was shogeg, certainly rely to be lenient. All this for eating; for benefit even per Rama permitted b'dieved.
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (45) Valid since, etc. — from this language it implies even if only a kezayit within time to eat a meal and it has taste of matzah one fulfills; see Peri Chadash and Magen Avraham that their view is one must eat entire mealtime so there is a kezayit matzah aside from spices; see above siman 453 seif 2 in Mishna Berurah regarding mixtures of grain with other species — l'chatchila we require majority grain; likewise here.
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Taz s.k. 1) Rather the main point is there is heating by day and night. Note: incidentally he also wrote thus, for the baraita explicitly states: in rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky, therefore the whole world is cold and springs boil — see there.
peri-megadim/1:א: No Taz; he raised: whoever has doubt afterward, etc.; Magen Avraham 1 agreed with Beit Yosef's explanation; Darkei Moshe in Beit Yosef's explanation in Beit Yosef: all drawn at night, even at beginning of night, immediately forbidden with no remedy — somewhat so in Tur. One who wants to satisfy all views should draw at bein ha shemashot itself.
peri-megadim/1:ב: Behold Rashi Pesachim 42a s.v. shelanu explained: in Nissan, rainy season, sun travels in lower sky and springs boil — therefore we leave overnight — end quote; the reason is explained: by day sun's heat strikes them because sun travels in lower sky near water and requires cooling — mayim shelanu, measure of average night (in Nissan day and night equal). He did not explain if drawn middle of night — perhaps permitted after six hours from detachment; all wrote for Rashi whether day or night we require 12 hours detached — whence? There is also another reason: perhaps at night sun travels under ground — not mentioned in Rashi; perhaps springs do not cool until detached 12 hours — see Levush and Rosh for Rashi leniency in river water more — I did not understand per Rashi in Gemara no distinction well and cistern; other explanation sun under ground at night — leniency in river water far from source cools in ground and attached source — Magen Avraham 6 unlike Rashi; therefore must say Rashi in responsum explained like R' Eliezer of Metz — also what Rosh wrote in Nissan sun does not travel in water — see Pesachim 94b; question what Rashi wrote in Nissan days sun travels in lower sky when 94b explains in Nissan, etc. For concern sun under ground at night as sages of nations hold Pesachim 94b — some poskim hold no remedy for all drawn at night that heated, etc.; Netziv note 1 questioned: if so no water fit for kneading, for yesterday attached in ground at night heated, etc.; one can say all that were 12 hours in ground by day cooled as Magen Avraham 1; also say drawn at night at moment of movement heats — no question from yesterday attached at night — see Magen Avraham 1; and some explain further; dispute sages of Israel and nations explained Pesachim 94b: for sages of Israel sunset is sun begins setting in sky thickness, measure of travel through sky thickness is hour minus quarter of hour — 58 and a half minutes; after this measure bein ha shemashot begins — 13 and a half minutes; total hour and fifth as explained Minchat Kohen Maamar Sheini ch. 2 32a; for sages of nations sunset is beginning to set under horizon, travel through earth thickness is sunset, then bein ha shemashot as above; Taz wrote under sky — typo, should be under ground as sages of nations and Beit Yosef; see Levush 61 wrote 11 springs always boil — for Rashi as we wrote. One afraid to satisfy all views should draw precisely at bein ha shemashot — time 13 and a half minutes after hour minus quarter from sunset beginning; knead after morning light only if full 12 hours detached passed — otherwise in leap year when night sometimes not long, forbidden until full 12 hours per Rashi; if night longer than 12 hours, forbidden before day per R' Yehuda bar Natan as said — Bach; see note 2 and Magen Avraham explained further.
peri-megadim/2:_: L'chatchila Taz; Magen Avraham notes 6 and 11 — Rashi Pesachim 42a explained in Nissan rainy season — great question, for 94b explains opposite — see note 1 here; main distinction between rivers: since far from source already cooled, unlike spring where sun travels at night, etc. — see there; so Magen Avraham explains further.
peri-megadim/4:_: Iron — Taz. Salt helps for tekufah — see Yoreh De'ah 116 end ch. 5 Ra'ah Chadash. In mayim shelanu forbidden to put our salt in them — fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz siman 462, 472 in Magen Avraham 7; explained there. Forbidden for gentile to draw for matzah of mitzvah — Peri Chadash: reason like preparing for mitzvah siman 462; b'dieved permitted; when drawing say for matzah of mitzvah — Kaf HaChayim notes 8, 9. And see Eliyah Rabbah in Magen Avraham note 16 from this. Iron or seal with cloth — implies sealing with cloth cannot harm as we find all engraved and sealed, etc. — see gloss 24 months; wooden vessel no concern — explained Magen Avraham note 10; Levush seif 7 requires study.
peri-megadim/5:_: Cistern Taz wrote meaning close to drawing; so Levush — apparently when lenient in pressure it is drawn close to bein ha shemashot; for Mechaber seif 1 while still day and did not stand 12 hours, then lenient in pressure — for R' Eliezer of Metz when drawn at bein ha shemashot permitted immediately, unlike drawing beginning of night per R' Eliezer of Metz no remedy forever per second explanation in Beit Yosef — therefore do not rely on this even in cistern in pressure; nevertheless in pressure all permit. Ateret Zekenim 11; Eliyah Rabbah 6: cistern or pipe called ra'er or hole at source — perhaps ra'er water nullified with cistern water — Magen Avraham 15; see Magen Avraham 11. Those wells with ra'er in houses where they brew beer and honey and put always dirty honey-beer vessels in well — prevent drawing from well, for honey is fruit juice; some say not nullified in 1000 — siman 462; Tur prefers drawing from pipe ra'er to put vessel there and drip there.
peri-megadim/6:א: Even Taz: first night if only water not left overnight, may l'chatchila knead to fulfill eating matzah mitzvah; appears same second night although moon fixes differently, both days one law — requires study perhaps not; although obligated to eat bread — Magen Avraham 488:9 whether Torah or rabbinic — see there.
peri-megadim/6:ב: Beit Yosef wrote Taz needs explanation. Mordechai chapter Kol Sha'ah 493: incident Pesach Sunday, tekufah also fell night before; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night; R' Yehuda HaChasid wrote no need to be concerned "keeper of mitzvah"; all baked only for next day, for Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow; second night too only for that day, not preparing for weekday. Per this text: nevertheless not concerned for tekufah fallen Motzei Shabbos night, drew at bein ha shemashot Motzei Shabbos as mayim shelanu and thought no prohibition in drawing, did not discard water, kneaded for day 1; likewise second night; they also hold when Pesach Sunday bake Pesach night lest matzah become stale — siman 458 Taz 1; R' Yehuda HaChasid not arguing but said they did well not discarding — keeper of mitzvah; this is Beit Yosef's language; simple they mean as those who say bake Pesach night itself — if bake Motzei Shabbos after chatzot not relevant; even per bake Pesach night wonder why not draw Friday; perhaps hold such not mayim shelanu; still wonder though tekufah fell Thursday night how permitted draw Shabbos for Yom Tov; you will say drawing not great exertion permitted; if so when tekufah fell Thursday night why concerned; they should draw Friday bein ha shemashot; further wonder tekufah: once three hours passed not tekufah hour; we concern only drinking at tekufah hour; perhaps all detached at tekufah harms afterward — end quote. Words hard to fit if text Thursday night; if text night before (mistakenly moved hei from b-lail) or explain Beit Yosef: tekufah fell Motzei Shabbos night because Pesach Sunday — "night before" means Motzei Shabbos; drew Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot with sunset as Beit Yosef beginning per R' Eliezer of Metz; simple for those who bake Pesach night — if not bake Motzei Shabbos after chatzot, already drew Thursday night belonging to Friday and baked, etc.; they also hold R' Eliezer of Metz if drawn close to sunset permitted immediately, not 12 hours unlike Rashi; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done not discarding — keeper of mitzvah; Beit Yosef asked why not draw Friday day instead bein ha shemashot Motzei Shabbos; answer perhaps hold all drawn by day no remedy with 12 hours waiting (still wonder better Thursday night bein ha shemashot than Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot); further asked should draw Friday bein ha shemashot lighter and not Motzei Shabbos where prohibition fixed — see Magen Avraham in Mishna Berurah shevut permitted bein ha shemashot if specifically Erev Shabbos not Motzei — see there; therefore text should be tekufah fell and delete she-lamed; heaven forbid I emend and delete she-lamed.
peri-megadim/6:ג: Bach's words require study — he too explains Beit Yosef had text tekufa night before — Motzei Shabbos as here; however what he wrote there they needed water for second Pesach night — although Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow, they should also for Yom Tov 1 — some imply they drew and waited 12 hours; then night 1 Pesach whence water; therefore drew Thursday night bein ha shemashot belonging to Friday; further per conclusion all detached harms water for day 1 — should explain drew for day 1 after Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot immediately at night beginning before springs boil per R' Eliezer of Metz and knead immediately as Tur there. Bach asked why discuss tekufah fell Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot nevertheless not concerned, drew immediately after sunset and kneaded immediately per R' Eliezer of Metz — if tekufah not fallen they would draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot as mayim shelanu l'chatchila precisely; R' Yehuda HaChasid disagrees said not well — should draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot keeper of mitzvah; Bach asked since tekufah fell they draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot now too; answer all detached harms — therefore waited after tekufah passed. Taz not satisfied with many difficulties as written; therefore other explanation; Mordechai text Thursday night; Rokeach Thursday night belonging to Friday; doubtful same — sometimes call Thursday night night of 5 belonging to 6 as Rama Thursday night Magen Avraham 4; what Shabbos 9 implies apparently baked Motzei Shabbos after chatzot as siman 461; tekufah Thursday night belonging to Friday; not concerned water detached at tekufah, no iron; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done — concludes Mordechai incident; all baked only for night 1 — Motzei Shabbos not Motzei; Pesach Sunday; Shabbos 9 proof.
peri-megadim/6:ד: Taz explained Mordechai text tekufah night before means Thursday night; "before" literally for Bach meant Sunday; reconcile Rokeach second night belonging to Thursday; they doubted because tekufah after bein ha shemashot how draw at tekufah hour — danger; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night — drew immediately after tekufah; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done; Beit Yosef challenged: still hard how depends on tekufah — without tekufah how permitted draw Thursday night for Yom Tov; answer drawing not great exertion permitted only because tekufah Thursday night they doubted and not concerned tekufah; we are Thursday night — should draw Friday bein ha shemashot better precisely l'chatchila and not violate tekufah preparation; final answer only on last question, etc. Know "kneaded with water drawn at night" — word "at night" separates "drawn" — meaning drawn at bein ha shemashot as law kneaded Pesach night. Taz Mordechai text Pesach Sunday tekufah night before — night before Pesach whether Thursday or Friday; Rokeach explains Thursday night 6 — only difference drew as law Thursday night as gloss seif 1 and baked Pesach night — they hold so siman 458; although water detached not concerned, baked, R' Yehuda HaChasid said well; all difficulties from Beit Yosef Shabbos how drew, etc.; but difficulty detached harms — Thursday night certainly no drawing as Rokeach like filling garden siman 338 (typo should be night before and Shabbos no draw); if tekufah relevance — Pesach other days detached knead Motzei after chatzot; rather "also" teaches Taz if drew Thursday night after tekufah one matter — two laws as said. Nevertheless Friday night bein ha shemashot shevut bein ha shemashot place of mitzvah Magen Avraham 4 only Shabbos no draw; Eliyah Rabbah 17 agrees Taz; drawn Thursday night means bein ha shemashot; some erred baked by day meaning Motzei because mitzvah beloved in its time proper Motzei.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 1 "in this all agree" — meaning Beit Yosef agrees with R' Eliyahu Mizrachi that per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's approach no remedy; but when drawn by day Beit Yosef disputes Mizrachi and holds even for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi there is remedy to wait until after night — see there.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Seif 3: whether water not left overnight forbidden. Bach wrote it appears from Or Zarua's words: all who say if one transgressed and kneaded, forbidden — in eating; in benefit permitted even hot — end quote.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: For bein ha shemashot. Baer Heitev; see Peri Chadach siman 259 seif 5: although Yoreh De'ah 36 when stood somewhat in house called lukewarm, nevertheless mayim shelanu are very cold; if heated like saliva warmth or like summer river water, has status of lukewarm and burn immediately — end quote; see Beit Efrayim on treifot in responsa compendium siman 80 length on this; explained there only when standing in house in summer we are particular, not Nissan days when Rashi Pesachim still rainy season, etc. — see there; may say whatever heated somewhat even not like saliva, do not knead — see there; concern this and place in cold place lest come to heat at all; see Mor VeKetzia in our northern lands in Nissan it is cold time, be lenient b'dieved water not left overnight in pressure — see there; appears all per posek's eyes per time and season.
shaarei-teshuvah/4:_: Thursday night Baer Heitev; see responsum Beit Efrayim siman 32: one who wants bake Sunday because Sunday has advantage in fitness — table and vessels cleanest, Motzei Shabbos everything washed well, hagalah and whitening working vessels; helpers in kneading and rolling, even hands cooled and strength renewed by Shabbos rest — this is need of mitzvah; lenient to permit drawing water Friday even if time of bein ha shemashot arrived; close to bein ha shemashot permit even without this fitness advantage — see there; see Beit Yehuda siman 57 also permits draw Friday and advance somewhat before bein ha shemashot; see there if left under open sky permitted bring morning because sun — not without need, like preparing for weekday since fit to drink today and good drink some — see there; Beit Yehuda 108 in name of Maharash Zur permitted draw via gentile Shabbos bein ha shemashot; so practiced Chida 87 — requires study.
shaarei-teshuvah/5:_: Iron. Baer Heitev on Beit Yosef's words; see Eliyah Rabbah there and responsum Beit Efrayim siman 32 — I wrote correct explanation of Beit Yosef's words with God's help — see there.
turei-zahav/2:_: L'chatchila one should draw, etc. Rashi wrote main stringency of water not left overnight is in springs and cisterns that boil, but not rivers — in Nissan sun does not travel in water, but sages were concerned for most towns that have only cistern and spring water; R' Avigdor wrote this is nothing, for even flowing rivers sun strikes by day and heats them; therefore better l'chatchila to draw from river when possible.
turei-zahav/3:_: One should not discard, etc. Reason in Mordechai: night of guarding is for Thursday; also wrote even other Pesach nights "He guards the simple" — heaven forbid mishap in mitzvah matzot — end quote; nevertheless appears other nights he may discard if easily without those waters, unlike night before Pesach which are for matzah of mitzvah — forbidden to discard, contemptuous of mitzvah, showing he holds mitzvah does not protect from mishap and verse "keeper of mitzvah knows no evil" is light in his eyes.
turei-zahav/5:_: Cistern. Room built beneath and around — they are as collected in a vessel and do not boil from sun traveling under ground, for building separates from ground; but Beit Yosef reported: these waters in winter are hot like well water; therefore do not be lenient unless pressure — meaning close to drawing.
turei-zahav/6:_: Even without pressure, etc. R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, Semag, and Semak permit even l'chatchila when impossible otherwise; appears first night one may rely so as not to nullify eating matzah mitzvah since b'shogeg permitted; not other days — eat other things. Beit Yosef brought Mordechai: incident Pesach Sunday, tekufah fell Thursday night before; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night; R' Yehuda HaChasid wrote no concern — keeper of mitzvah; Mordechai after: baked only for day 1, Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow; Rokeach brought this law but there writes tekufa fell Thursday night only. It appears he understood tekufa fell Shabbos night, drew at night, baked Motzei matzah — night 1 Pesach; thus Mordechai explained; they did not want draw Motzei night per Rashi requiring 12 hours always, not concerned tekufa at drawing hour; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done keeper of mitzvah — implies bake Pesach night when Sunday; otherwise only Motzei bake no place for Mordechai; Beit Yosef further even so Mordechai not settled — wonder why crossed tekufa danger, not draw Friday day; answered perhaps hold by day no remedy per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Mizrachi — Beit Yosef; perhaps hold such not mayim shelanu — Mizrachi; Bach asked why concerned Shabbos drawing tekufa — implies without tekufa no doubt; even without, Shabbos drawing prohibition; you will say such permitted Shabbos — then how draw afterward at night; why concerned tekufa at all since not at kneading hour; answered hold all water detached at tekufah hour dangerous even after — not answering other questions to explain Beit Yosef per his understanding. Mahari Weil other explanation per Beit Yosef — I did not reconcile; truth in Mordechai unlike Beit Yosef: drew Motzei Friday night only after drawing that night or Shabbos night tekufa — no difference; why Mordechai wrote Thursday night not Thursday 6: drew as law Motzei Friday bein ha shemashot, baked Yom Tov night — teaches two laws: tekufah does not harm what they kneaded for mitzvah though passed in detached; second that night baked only for Yom Tov 1 — two laws independent, both occurred — therefore Mordechai wrote also fell, etc., another novelty there; Shabbos obviously no drawing as Rokeach like filling garden end Eruvin — all Bach's questions inapplicable — in my humble opinion.
turei-zahav/1:_: One may not knead, etc. Thus the Rosh: because in Nissan days the springs boil and it is still the rainy season and the sun travels in the lower sky — therefore one fills from evening and they cool until morning. R' Avigdor wrote: according to this reason, one who draws in the morning and leaves until evening is fine; but R' Eliyahu Mizrachi explained: because at night the sun travels under the earth, therefore they have no remedy except not to be attached at night; therefore those who draw at the beginning of the night are permitted immediately and forbidden to draw after the beginning of the night — end quote. Thus Semag: R' Eliezer of Metz says even l'chatchila one may knead with them when impossible, as said at the end of chapter Kol Sha'ah: Rav Matna expounded in Papunia — a woman should knead only in mayim shelanu; tomorrow they all brought their jugs to him, thinking shelanu meant Rav Matna's water; he told them: I mean water from my house — meaning they left overnight; and we do not find they fasted from eating. Rashi explained the reason for mayim shelanu: because the sun travels in Nissan days which is still rainy season, etc.; according to his reason, drawing in the morning and leaving until evening is permitted; and from Papunia there is no proof — but the reason must be because at night the sun travels under the ground; therefore one who draws at the beginning of the night is permitted immediately; therefore forbidden after drawing after the beginning of the night — end quote. Rambam and R' Yehuda bar Natan ruled in commentary on Pesachim: forbidden to bake before dawn; if they baked, the baked product should be forbidden lest the end of the night causes cooling — however this prohibition applies only to Rashi, not R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — end quote. R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote on what Semag wrote \"we do not find they fasted from eating\": it appears it was during Pesach when they kneaded in water not left overnight; when he said \"I mean from my house,\" he presumably permitted kneading in water not left overnight — you will ask: on that day they ate no matzah but fruits — why did the Talmud not mention this to teach us? One cannot say he permitted the baked matzot that were shogeg in kneading, for only \"if one transgressed and kneaded\" did Rav Ashi forbid, but shogeg not, and he would not permit l'chatchila, for presumably they destroyed all their matzot before coming to him because of chametz prohibition (and per this reasoning the Talmud need not mention shogeg is permitted); if it was the Shabbos before Pesach, what of \"we do not find they fasted\" — they already ate chametz four hours on the first night, and in the evening they could already knead with water drawn in the morning after 12 hours per Rashi, or draw at beginning of night permitted immediately per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, etc.; but the question is: whence that exposition was during Pesach — perhaps on Shabbos before Pesach, and he permitted on the first night for fulfillment of eating matzah, not during Pesach where there is no mitzvah fulfillment — end quote Mizrachi's words. Objection on him per his reasoning: he asked perhaps it was Shabbos before Pesach — why did he need to ask because of matzah fulfillment; he should have asked perhaps he expounded Shabbos before Pesach not to draw except mayim shelanu and they thought Rav Matna's water, and on the first night he said draw on the first night per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi who need not distinguish first night from rest of Pesach — forced distinction as Beit Yosef wrote on him: wherever chametz prohibition applies there is no distinction; or he should have asked from what he himself said to prove R' Eliyahu Mizrachi held the exposition was during Pesach not Shabbos before, and therefore asked whence for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it was not Shabbos before — Beit Yosef already sensed this. It appears to me on the contrary R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds the exposition was Shabbos before, as all who want to learn Pesach laws before Pesach; what Mizrachi wrote they already ate chametz four hours on the first night — I wonder why Mizrachi did not analyze R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words \"we do not find they fasted from eating\" — why not say they fasted alone and this \"from eating\" is extra language; rather it appears not a full fast all day but on mealtime which is beginning of the night itself, for they hurry to eat lest children sleep, as siman 472; and he holds as Tur siman 458 in the name of R' Yehuda HaKohen: on Yom Tov night one should not trouble on Yom Tov to bake matzah — therefore it fits here: you will ask they drew beginning of Pesach night and delayed in drawing, kneading, arranging, baking — mealtime which is on the first night by law would be lost; therefore he said we do not find they fasted from eating — meaning the proper mealtime; rather certainly he permitted kneading immediately in water not left overnight. Granted for Rashi no proof — one could say they had other water at home and waited until after chatzot and baked matzah after 12 hours and ate in evening; but per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi there is proof as written; thus other difficulties of Mizrachi that Beit Yosef brought are settled. Mizrachi wrote further: per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi he must hold if drawn before beginning of night while sun still on earth, forbidden to knead, because they must be attached in earth by day when earth is cold and cools them — otherwise no proof from Papunia even per his words that we can say they left what was drawn by day; and from \"one who draws at beginning of night\" it implies if drawn before beginning or after, no — end quote. Beit Yosef disagrees: if so how does it say one may knead only in mayim shelanu — what is night's work: if drawn while sun on earth or after beginning of night, even ours forbidden; if at beginning of night, even not ours permitted; rather should have written one may knead only in what was drawn at bein ha shemashot; therefore he explained per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi three divisions: drawn at bein ha shemashot — permitted immediately; drawn after beginning of night — wait another day and night; drawn by day — wait that day and following night; and when he said mayim shelanu until they stood one full night and cooled in coldness — when drawn after beginning of night the reason is heat of sun under ground; when drawn by day, although earth is cold, they do not cool from boiling until 12 hours pass; and since the world is hot by day and water heats when drawn by movement as Rif and Ran wrote, they do not cool until one night; but drawn at bein ha shemashot, although they heat when drawn by movement, R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds since the world is cold then they cool immediately. Therefore \"one who draws at beginning of night permitted immediately\" means then permitted immediately; but if drawn before beginning while sun on earth or after beginning, forbidden until full night passes. And \"they have no remedy except not to be at night attached\" — not that no remedy forever, rather remedy of 12 hours detached does not help when drawn by day or after beginning of night, only one full night — end Beit Yosef; many questions on Rabbeinu Yehuda's explanation, for night's stringency is from one of two ways: either because in measure of night the boiling in them cools as Rashi, or at night itself there is boiling per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi; per Beit Yosef's words of R' Eliyahu Mizrachi when drawn by day they heated from movement and need one night to cool; when drawn at night they boil from the night per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — he should hold two powers in that night: cooling and fixing boiling drawn by day, and second boiling of water attached at night — why did R' Eliyahu Mizrachi write drawn at bein ha shemashot permitted immediately, whence — since anyway there is boiling from drawing movement, certainly here too needs full night to cool like by day. What Beit Yosef wrote: since bein ha shemashot is cold they cool immediately is very astonishing — whence for Rambam boiling cools in one moment as soon as they draw; and since day's boiling by movement and bein ha shemashot's boiling are equal, why does drawing by day not suffice to wait until bein ha shemashot and cool as drawn at bein ha shemashot; a fortiori drawing by day whose time is longer should help bein ha shemashot's cooling for day's drawing boiling, since bein ha shemashot's cooling helps what was drawn at bein ha shemashot when boilings are equal — I do not know place to settle our rabbi Beit Yosef's words and why he troubled to explain \"they have no remedy\" that R' Eliyahu Mizrachi mentioned and why he asked what does Semag bring proof from Papunia per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and not Rashi — granted for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi no proof, perhaps drawn at beginning of night; Beit Yosef explained Semag's proof: Gemara needed this incident of Papunia which is not for need — implying it teaches permission to knead in water not left overnight; granted for Rashi no proof — one could say it teaches leniency when drawn morning and wait until evening, unlike R' Eliyahu Mizrachi who is not satisfied with that — if so certainly Gemara wrote this incident to inform us water not left overnight is permitted when impossible — these are Beit Yosef's words though not his language. I wonder why the rabbi here deviated from his path of truth everywhere and inclined to sharp pepper and explained what did not occur to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — he had proof from not finding they fasted from eating, and Rabbeinu Yehuda discarded that proof and wrote another proof: why Gemara needed this incident not mentioned in R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words; and per Beit Yosef's pilpul we too say for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi no proof — Gemara teaches mayim shelanu means water from his house — meaning night itself requires, not measure of overnight like Rashi where even by day helps; this certainly should be informed in Talmud; Mahari Weil also explained for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi overnight of night helps for drawn by day and washed his hands to explain Mizrachi who holds so; he raged at Beit Yosef who explained Mizrachi's words as mistaken — rather Mizrachi also holds so, except drawing at night he explains they have no remedy forever; astonishing, for Mizrachi explicitly wrote if drawn before beginning or after, no — clear before is like after with no distinction. And no reason ever to distinguish invalidity from day's boiling and night's boiling — who is the prophet to tell us there is distinction — Gemara did not mention this at all, only we require overnight without condition. It appears to me Mizrachi's explanation per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi is clear truth: for Rashi there is no boiling for night because it is night, but because rainy season and springs always boil day and night; night came only to fix boiling — cool at night time; thus also waiting by day measure of night suffices.
