R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds night mentioned here is because there is boiling at night since sun travels under earth; by day obviously sun on earth and certainly boiling — Gemara teaches also at night there is boiling; night's boiling certainly not specifically when hot all night — if less than full night we do not say so — if so why insist overnight in detached, suffices part of night in detached; rather certainly also part of night has heat, at least most of night; this cannot be clarified — therefore sages required detached all night; not literally all night unless drawn at very beginning they had not yet received night's boiling in that moment — therefore R' Eliyahu Mizrachi permitted drawn at beginning of night implying literally at night but small measure. Tur wrote one who draws evening until sunset permitted immediately — comes to distance further from transgression, beware drawing even at beginning of night because of erring; it turns out Beit Yosef should have written one may knead only in water drawn at bein ha shemashot — truth is not so, for even drawn at beginning of night permitted, that too is called mayim shelanu; prohibition only in drawn large part of night; by day obvious to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi forbidden, not for reason Mizrachi said R' Eliyahu Mizrachi requires all day cold from earth's cold — one can answer when drawn by day placed in cellar or cave they cool too as Beit Yosef wrote; and if heat by day what does earth's cold help — only wonder; rather main point: heat by day sun on earth heats water; at night sun under earth heats; no permission except hour without heat — beginning of night, and all the more bein ha shemashot before it; all forbidden drawn in hour of boiling day or after beginning of night have no remedy — like hot water cooling never helps; all this R' Eliyahu Mizrachi learned from Talmud \"one may knead only in mayim shelanu\" — had it said by day permitted, should have said only drawn by day; had it said part of night forbidden at beginning, should have said only drawn at bein ha shemashot or one may not knead water drawn at night except certainly also at night there is permission — beginning; therefore said shelanu meaning like way of overnight called see most of night called overnight for person too; we learn if drawn at beginning of night properly called mayim shelanu; R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Semag words are correct and clear: R' Eliyahu Mizrachi said proof l'chatchila permit water not left overnight when impossible — otherwise what did Papunia do after learning prohibition to eat evening at matzah mealtime — beginning of night immediately when needed to draw, knead, bake — not worth hiding; Talmud owner should inform they pushed mitzvah time for this — rather certainly permitted even l'chatchila when needed; Semag words on R' Yehuda bar Natan forbidden bake before dawn lest end of night causes cooling — on this: nevertheless this prohibition only Rashi — from tying night to cooling implies R' Yehuda bar Natan has other explanation in Rashi's words: boiling because rainy season and springs boil, need cooling, cooling not time-dependent but specifically at night when cold; also at night itself perhaps specifically end of night causes cooling when north wind blows as Semak — therefore Semag wrote nevertheless this prohibition only Rashi — \"nevertheless\" implies R' Yehuda bar Natan does not hold like Rashi that Semag brought first that 12 hours depends, rather specifically at night from night's cooling they become permitted; but for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi this prohibition does not apply — end of night for cooling — for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi we do not tie cooling to night, night used only for prohibition; if drawn after beginning forbidden forever; if at beginning no prohibition — why need dawn; we are raised to settle Rabbeinu Yehuda's difficulty on Mizrachi in Hagahot Maimoniyot ch. 1 R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words and \"some forbid\" when drawn while still day even if left all night afterward — Mizrachi's view is R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's view; what \"some forbid\" — I wonder, for Beit Yosef rejected that view as his proof that forbidden even with overnight when drawn while still day; behold we explicitly find this view \"some forbid\"; why not attribute also to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi; Gemara's \"some forbid\" is no contradiction to Mizrachi, for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi did not explicitly forbid while still day as \"some forbid\"; find Tur siman 461 after Rabbenu Tam wrote \"some forbid\" — Rabbenu Tam himself just did not mention in explanation; our words in Semak siman 291: one may knead only in mayim shelanu; some stringent to draw water between day and night; Rabbi R' Yitzchak says Torah was not given to ministering angels; further should have taught shelanu all night — rather overnight only from midnight until dawn when north wind blows — end quote; explained as above: \"some forbid\" is R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's view — permitted at beginning of night, stringent not to draw even at beginning, only between day and night; R' Yitzchak says since by law permitted at beginning and we are not angels to measure precisely when begins, certainly by law from midnight until dawn. For law Beit Yosef ruled draw while still day or bein ha shemashot and do not knead until their entire night passes — \"while still day\" is his view explaining R' Eliyahu Mizrachi: drawn by day has remedy next night; per Mizrachi drawn by day or after beginning of night no remedy forever — this explanation is absolute truth as written; therefore do not practice drawing while still day although not forbidden to draw while still day and leave afterward — one may rely on Rashi; nevertheless l'chatchila avoid until sunset; delaying somewhat profits more, for even at beginning of night full permission as written; whoever doubts sunset should delay and not advance — and so Mordechai end chapter Kol Sha'ah: ancestors drew after sunset; Behag wrote mitzvah to fill water between suns and stars — end quote; so practice halacha l'maaseh.
ateret-zekenim/5:_: It is customary not to, etc. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape the faces of the matzot with salt water and return them to the oven as they do on chol ha'moed with salt water and eggs; and specifically on chol ha'moed it is permitted to scrape, but on the first two nights it is forbidden; and even to dip them in salt that the Yerushalmi permitted as below siman 475 — people refrain; and in this too there is concern because of do not forsake, etc. Nevertheless in this too b'dieved one need not be concerned even if he scraped after baking in salt water and eggs and spices as on chol ha'moed, for this scraping is no worse than spices with which matzah was baked through which one fulfills the obligation of matzah (my teacher in Bach).
baer-heitev/1:ב: Not harmful. And even if they stood in the sun. Beit Yosef and Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/1:ג: To cover them. Specifically an earthenware or wood vessel and the like — covering helps; but if they are in a glass vessel, covering does not help. Kaf HaChayim — see there.
baer-heitev/1:ה: Iron. One takes new or clean iron and hangs it on a cord in the water, but one does not put his hand in the water, for the hand heats the water. In the rest of the year one places salt or a seal. Darkei Moshe, Magen Avraham. Taz wrote: it appears to me that on other nights, if one did not place iron in them to guard from the tekufah, one may pour them out if one can easily be without that water — which is not so with these waters of matzah of the mitzvah: it is forbidden to pour out, for it appears contemptuous of the verse "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil" — see there; and Kaf HaChayim practice filtering water — Maharil. Mateh Moshe wrote one should not take a vessel to draw water that had honey or fruit juice in it, for fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz as siman 462. (And likewise one should not take a copper vessel — Magen Avraham — and I have not seen practice so.) It appears to me that through boiling it is permitted. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/2:א: In a cistern (susternah). This is what they call in Talmudic language a pit — water collected in a building in the ground where the building separates it from the ground and it is also covered above, so it is as if they are drawn; one should not compare this to what we call in foreign language ar'ar kastin, for although it is covered above, one may not draw from it to use close to drawing because every hour and moment flows into it from the river. However, if one wishes to leave them overnight like other water and draw at its time, it is permitted to draw under the pipe or what they call in foreign language ar'ar, like from a river or a well drawn from it; and likewise from the kastin itself if it is covered. Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/3:א: Its copper rim. Rashi explained the rim is thick and there is no difference between copper and earthenware — Magen Avraham. Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote R' Yitzchak the White would not allow kneading in water that was in a copper vessel that heats the water — there was an incident and other rabbis forbade likewise. However, practice is to knead in copper vessels, as in Knesset HaGedolah and Kaf HaChayim s.k. 10. Or Zaru'a wrote an incident came before my elders, may they rest in Eden: one placed mayim matzah in a warm winter room; he asked if the vessel was hot when they took from it; he said no — and permitted.
baer-heitev/3:ג: B'shogeg. And he has no other dough — Magen Avraham. Taz wrote on the first night one may rely so as not to nullify the positive mitzvah of eating matzah, but not other days — rather he eats other things. (And Kaf HaChayim implies the opposite for matzah of the mitzvah in any case one should not take it — see there.)
baer-heitev/6:א: With caraway. Kimmel in Ashkenaz language.
baer-heitev/6:ד: Lime. This is live lime; but lime in a wall that already dried and hardened like stone — it appears plainly it does not forbid. Shevut Yaakov part 2 siman 13.
beer-hagolah/1:ג: Rashi and Ba'al HaHalachot Gedolot and most of the poskim
beer-hagolah/2:א: Orchot Chayim in the name of the Ra'avad
beer-hagolah/4:_: Semag in the name of R' Yechiel and Semak
beer-hagolah/6:ב: Tur in the name of Rokeach; there 20; and pepper; and prohibition of spices — he wrote all of it in the name of the Ra'avad
beur-hagra/1:נ: One may not pour out. As written "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil" — and Taz.
chok-yaakov/2:א: Cistern. This is what Talmud calls a pit — water collected in a building in the ground separated from the ground and covered above, as if drawn; not comparable to ar'ar kastin covered above — do not draw close to drawing because constantly flows from river; but if leaving overnight like other water, permitted to draw under pipe or ar'ar like river or well or kastin itself if covered.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] One may not knead, etc. I found our text points shelanu with kamatz under the lamed, not patach, lest it mean him alone like lanu in Gibeah — end quote.
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [6] [Levush] It is a building, etc. Chok Yaakov wrote one should not compare to ar'ar kastin because constantly flows from river; however if one wishes to leave overnight, permitted to draw under pipe like kastin itself — end quote; requires slight analysis: also in cistern water always flows from depth.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ד: And b'dieved Bach is lenient if drawn at night. This is called b'dieved.
magen-avraham/1:ב: Not harmful. And even if they stood in the sun (Beit Yosef, Eliyah Rabbah); siman 459 seif 65.
magen-avraham/1:ה: From rivers. Because the sun travels in Nissan days under the ground and therefore wells boil; but melting of snow and rain always boils.
magen-avraham/1:ו: And not from wells. Because the sun travels under the ground.
magen-avraham/1:ז: One may not pour out. For "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil."
magen-avraham/1:ט: Iron. One does not put his hand in the water, for the hand heats — only hang on a cord (Maharil); rest of year salt or seal (Hagahot Maimoniyot, Darkei Moshe). Practice filters water (Maharil). Mateh Moshe: do not take vessel that had honey or fruit juice — fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz siman 462. (Boiling permitted — it appears.) Also not in copper vessel that heats — end quote; however I have seen kneading in copper troughs — Semag see there.
magen-avraham/2:_: Cistern. Building separates from ground and covered above — as if drawn.
magen-avraham/3:ג: In time of pressure. Bach explained: if no other water, permitted to knead; disagreed with Shulchan Aruch; it appears Shulchan Aruch did not intend to permit except if kneaded b'dieved and no other dough — Rama refers to this; wrote even without pressure permit if transgressed b'shogeg, etc. — see above seif 1.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) One may not knead, etc. — whether matzah of the mitzvah or other matzot.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) Whether river water — although not from springs and reasons above do not apply, nevertheless be stringent also to cool them because sun's heat by day warmed them somewhat.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (27) One should not be lenient, etc. — for we see water inside is not cold at all; one can say since building attached to ground, although paved, nevertheless heats from sun traveling under ground — therefore needs overnight like other waters unless pressure. When water does not flow under pavement; but if flows under pavement or constant pipe like ar'ar kastin always pouring from pipes — do not be lenient even in pressure, for water in building connects with ground water. Water in pool certainly not lenient even in pressure — not covered below only above — Peri Megadim.
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (29) In hot water — even if became lukewarm as below; even if completely cooled, some forbid kneading because once hot; some dispute and permit; rely on them in pressure or great loss if transgressed and kneaded much matzah.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (39) Knead with them — specifically if water mixed before kneading and nullified; putting one part in two in mayim shelanu is forbidden even b'dieved — study if mixed intentionally.
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (41) In matzah — before baking; after baking certainly permitted to scrape matzah faces in salt water and return to oven as on chol ha'moed; nevertheless for matzah of mitzvah on both nights be careful.
beur-hagra/1:י: And when carrying, etc. See Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/1:ל: L'chatchila, etc. As above, springs boil — which is not so with rivers:
beur-hagra/1:מ: But when the rivers. As written there that the sun travels in Nissan in the mountains in order to thaw the snows and they become lukewarm:
beur-hagra/1:ס: And also forbidden. For it is a preparer of mitzvah; and see above siman 464 as written:
beur-hagra/1:ע: And even. Lest one put chametz into it:
beur-hagra/2:ב: And one should not be lenient. For they nevertheless heat from their connection to the ground — see Beit Yosef:
beur-hagra/3:ה: And there are those who disagree. According to Rashi who explains drawn water means from a kettle, etc., as above — thus the question does not apply at all to water not left overnight:
beur-hagra/3:ז: And even without, etc. Since there are those who permit even intentionally, as above:
chatam-sofer/3:_: (There in seif 6 in the gloss) And pepper — Mishna Berurah; see my responsa part 6 Orach Chayim siman 109 [regarding wheat in which were found among them things like small sharp fresh shoots like shoots; when ground with the wheat there is concern for fruit juice and sharp things causing leavening, but it is a minor matter, etc., and he wrote at the end of the responsum: in the case before us, if the wheat is ground and in them something squeezed and liquefied — even one drop is not nullified, as it says nullified in majority or nullified its sharpness, only if one finds a little flour at its side and it clumps and becomes small balls; and since it is a leavening matter, if it stands a day or two days there is concern it will become chametz for the dough; and further they do not mix in kneading and remain visible in matzah, and on Pesach it harms and one eats it — therefore better to select the wheat well and then sift the flour slowly so if there are such balls they remain above in the sifter; nevertheless if they did not do so one should not presume harm and forbid b'dieved — poor people will eat and be satisfied] and see further my responsa part 6 Orach Chayim siman 129:
chok-yaakov/1:ב: Under the ceiling. And that he did not mention to cover with a cloth as written below — because they must be in an exposed place where air rules, as the Mechaber wrote in the name of Or Zarua; if one covers with cloth they become warm. According to this it is not correct that people are careful to cover water specifically even in cold weather; we must say therefore covering at night is ineffective because we are concerned he might forget to bring them in for a long time by day and they will heat via the cloth or covering if not covered well — unlike below when carrying water only via transit, any covering helps:
chok-yaakov/1:ד: One must cover them. Specifically in earthenware or wood vessel and the like — covering helps; but if they are in a glass vessel, covering does not help, for since the sun shines through glass it heats more than if exposed — as in chapter 2 of Beitza daf 33a — see Rashi there and above siman 472; requires study:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 4: water not left overnight that was nullified — one in two in our water to knead with them; Mishna Berurah. Know that he specified specifically one in two and not elsewhere — see in my composition on Yoreh De'ah siman 109 explained well with God's help, and it is in the printed composition seif 6 — see there and understand:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] [Levush] Before sunrise, etc. And if he did not bring them in at dawn — if they did not stand so long that they heated, it is not harmful (Rama); and even if they stood in the sun (Magen Avraham). The Levush whom he omitted appears he relied on what he wrote at end of the seif that in a brief time one should not be concerned so much. There was an incident: someone placed mayim shelanu in a warm winter room and asked our teacher the Gaon, may his memory be for a blessing, if the vessel was hot when they took from it; they answered no and permitted:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (b) There. One may knead only in mayim shelanu. Therefore shelanu with kamatz under the lamed; but one should not read it with patach, for then it speaks of him alone like lanu in Gibeah — end quote. See there; or Aleph; meaning: if with kamatz it will be weak like lanu in Gibeah that returns on others, and here too it returns on the water; but if with patach it will be with dagesh like lanu in Gibeah speaking of itself.
levushei-serad/1:_: Shulchan Aruch seif 3: one may not knead in hot water, etc. The measure of heat — see Peri Megadim siman 259 seif 8 that it is like saliva warmth or like water drawn in summer from the river; if one kneaded with them it burns immediately — see there:
mishnah-berurah/1:ע: (16) From the rivers — because the sun travels in Nissan days under the ground, and therefore wells boil somewhat; unlike rivers, for although at their source they boil, nevertheless when drawn to a distance they cool:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif 1: one should draw. And it is fitting to say with the mouth that he draws for the sake of the mitzvah — minor matter:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/4:_: Seif 4: water not left overnight that was nullified. And if a little of our water mixed into water not left overnight — it appears one needs afterward majority against all the water, for those of ours also already became warm. Eshkol Avraham above siman 150 s.k. 7:
turei-zahav/4:_: Iron. One should be careful with the iron placed in the water to place it in a manner that he will not need to put his hand in at the time of kneading, for his hand heats the water; also the iron should be clean (so too Maharil):
